title: Portrait of Mark Antony (Vatican Museums bust)
description: Marble portrait bust in the Vatican Museums, Sala dei Busti. Often identified as Mark Antony based on physiognomic comparison with coin portraits, but the identification is not universally accepted. The heavy brow, thick neck, and individualized features are consistent with late Republican veristic portraiture.
location: Vatican Museums, Rome, Sala dei Busti, Inv. 592.

title: Antony portrait on silver denarius (legionary coinage)
description: Silver denarius from Antony's legionary series. Obverse: war galley with ANT AVG III VIR R P C. Reverse: legionary eagle between two standards with LEG (number). Antony's portrait appears on other contemporary issues (RRC 496, 521, 533, 536, 542).

title: Antony-Cleopatra tetradrachm
description: Silver tetradrachm from an eastern mint. Obverse: diademed bust of Cleopatra with the legend 'Queen Cleopatra.' Reverse: bare head of Mark Antony with Armenian tiara and the legend 'Antony, having conquered Armenia.'

title: Relief panel of Cleopatra and Caesarion at Dendera Temple (Antony absent)
description: Temple of Hathor at Dendera, Egypt. The rear wall of the temple features a colossal relief of Cleopatra VII and Caesarion making offerings to the gods. The relief was carved during the Ptolemaic period when Antony was allied with Cleopatra, but Antony himself does not appear in the relief.
